'''DeJuan Lamont Blair''' (born April 22, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]] from 2007 to 2009. Blair entered the [[2009 NBA draft]] where he was selected as the 37th overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for seven seasons with the Spurs, [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[Washington Wizards]]. Blair also played in the [[NBA Development League]] and overseas in Russia, China and Argentina.

==Early life==
The oldest of four children (one of whom died in infancy), Blair grew up in [[Pittsburgh]]'s [[Hill District]].<ref name="O'Neil profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=3865922 |title=Just a short walk from home, local boy Blair makes good with Panthers |first=Dana |last=O'Neil |publisher=ESPN |date=January 29, 2008 |access-date=February 26, 2009}}</ref> Although he was the smallest of his siblings at birth, he was the largest child in his class by the time that he started at Manchester Academic Charter School, where he attended kindergarten through eighth grade. Both of his parents played basketball at [[Schenley High School]], which was located in North Oakland/Schenley Heights until 2008, and his uncle ran the nearby Ammons Recreation Center, where he learned to play the game.<ref name="O'Neil profile" />

==High school career==
Blair attended the same school as his parents, [[Schenley High School]]. While there, he played for the basketball team and scored 1,563 career points and finished with an overall 103–16 team record, including a 57–0 record within the Pittsburgh City League. He was named the [[Associated Press|AP]] player of the state and made first-team all-state his junior and senior year. Blair led Schenley to the 2007 PIAA Class 4A state championship, the first state title for a City League team since 1978; in the final against [[Chester High School (Chester, Pennsylvania)|Chester]], he had 18 points, 23 rebounds, and 6 blocked shots.<ref name="O'Neil profile" /> He was also named Pittsburgh City League Player of the year three times.

Blair also played in the summer leagues at Pittsburgh's Kennard Park and played a championship game in which his team played against a team led by future [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]] [[quarterback]] [[Terrelle Pryor]], who was also a highly regarded basketball prospect.<ref name="O'Neil profile" />

After two surgeries during his high school years, Blair was left without any [[anterior cruciate ligament]]s (ACLs) in his knees.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://primary.slate.com/articles/news_and_politics/explainer/2009/11/no_ligaments_no_problem.html |title=No Ligaments, No Problem |first=Juliet |last=Lapidos |work=Slate.com |date=November 3, 2009 |access-date=January 13, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304102121/http://primary.slate.com/articles/news_and_politics/explainer/2009/11/no_ligaments_no_problem.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Blair was heavily recruited coming out of high school. Besides Pitt, other schools pursuing him included [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]], [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]].

His parents admitted that if they had their way, Blair would have gone to Tennessee because they liked the Volunteers' coach [[Bruce Pearl]], and thought it would be a good idea for their son to leave the city. Blair himself had problems making up his mind; while considering as many as 18 different [[athletic scholarship|scholarship]] offers, he was so confused that one day he threw his [[mobile phone|cell phone]] across a room, breaking it.<ref name="O'Neil profile" />

However, [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pitt]] coach [[Jamie Dixon]] recognized the importance of Blair's maternal grandmother, Donna Saddler, who had played a major role in his upbringing, and on the first day he was allowed to contact Blair, he called Saddler, asking to come to her house. She told Dixon that they were having a [[family reunion]] at the house that day, and invited him to come, which he did. When Dixon was down to his last scholarship in the 2007 recruiting cycle, he called her, telling her that Blair would need to take the scholarship at that time. In the end, Saddler made the decision for him, telling him "Pitt is it." She liked Dixon and the proximity of her home to the school. Also, she was well aware that Pitt would be losing starting center [[Aaron Gray]] to graduation, which would have made Blair a likely candidate to start if he attended. He officially announced his decision to attend Pitt at the Ammons Recreation Center, where his basketball journey began, and became the first City League player to play for Pitt since Darelle Porter from 1987 to 1991.<ref name="O'Neil profile" />

==College career==

===2007–08===
Blair became the starter during his freshman year at the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. He made the [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American Freshman team]], helping the Panthers win the [[2008 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East Conference tournament]] and securing a fourth seed in the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]]. The Panthers won their first-round game against Oral Roberts, but lost in the second round to fifth-seeded [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]]. Blair was named the Big East Co-Rookie of the Year, earned All-Big East honorable mention honors, and was named the Big East Rookie of the Week three times. He also set Pitt freshman school records for most starts (36), rebounds (337), and field goals made (168), and became the first freshman in Pitt history to finish with 400+ points and 300+ rebounds.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=DeJuan Blair Bio|url=http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/blair_dejuan00.html|work=PittsburghPanthers.com|access-date=January 13, 2016|archive-date=September 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908061816/http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/blair_dejuan00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===2008–09===
In the [[2008–09 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|2008–09]] season, Blair averaged 15.7 points and 12.3 rebounds per game, helping Pittsburgh earn a number one seed in the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Blair and [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|Connecticut]] center [[Hasheem Thabeet]] shared co-[[Big East Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] honors for the 2008–09 season. He was a consensus [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|first-team All-American]] selection by the [[Associated Press]], [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] and ''[[The Sporting News]]''. He also made the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC's]] second team<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/awards/allamerica/2000-09.html |title=USBWA MEN'S ALL-AMERICANS – 2000–09 |work=sportswriters.net |access-date=January 13, 2016 |archive-date=February 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204095140/http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/awards/allamerica/2000-09.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=526662 |title=Sporting News 2008–09 College Basketball All-Americans |work=SportingNews.com |date=March 12, 2009 |access-date=March 17, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090314074333/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=526662 |archive-date=March 14, 2009 }}</ref> and finished tied for second with [[Tyler Hansborough]] (two votes each) for the 2009 [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year]], an award which was won by the eventual first overall pick in the 2009 NBA draft, [[Blake Griffin]] (66 votes).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2009-04-03/oklahomas-griffin-named-ap-player-year|title=Oklahoma's Griffin Named AP Player Of The Year|work=NCAA.com|date=April 3, 2009|access-date=January 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304194945/http://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2009-04-03/oklahomas-griffin-named-ap-player-year|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In April 2009, Blair declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/pitt-s-dejuan-blair-to-declare-for-nba-draft-1.1217978|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160302210453/http://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/pitt-s-dejuan-blair-to-declare-for-nba-draft-1.1217978|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 2, 2016|title=Pitt's Dejuan Blair to declare for NBA draft|work=NewsDay.com|date=April 8, 2009|access-date=February 20, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2009/news/story?id=4052755|title=Pitt's Blair declares for NBA draft|publisher=ESPN|date=May 13, 2009|access-date=February 20, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===San Antonio Spurs (2009–2013)===
[[File:Blair muscleman.JPG|thumb|right|Blair with the Spurs in 2010]]
On June 25, 2009, Blair was selected by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] with 37th overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062509aaa.html|title=PITT'S SAM YOUNG AND DEJUAN BLAIR SELECTED IN 2009 NBA DRAFT|work=PittsburghPanthers.com|date=June 25, 2009|access-date=February 20, 2016|archive-date=March 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305050300/http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062509aaa.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> His stock fell because of questions surrounding his durability and knee surgeries. On July 17, he signed a four-year deal with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fittipaldo|first=Ray|title=Blair, Spurs reach a deal|date=July 17, 2009|work=Post-Gazette.com|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/Pitt/2009/07/17/Blair-Spurs-reach-a-deal/stories/200907170193|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017163715/http://www.post-gazette.com/stories/sports/pitt-big-east/blair-spurs-reach-a-deal-349906/|archive-date=October 17, 2012|url-status=live|access-date=July 17, 2009}}</ref> In his first NBA game, he posted a double-double with 14 points and 11 rebounds in 23 minutes against the [[New Orleans Hornets]] on October 28, thus becoming just the third Spurs rookie, along with [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]] and [[Tim Duncan]], to record a double-double in his debut with the team. He later recorded 28 points and 21 rebounds in 31 minutes against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on January 13, 2010, becoming first NBA rookie since Tim Duncan in the 1997–98 season to post a 20–20 game. In the team's final regular season game, he recorded 27 points, a season-high 23 rebounds, 4 assists and 3 steals in 37 minutes against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on April 14, becoming the first rookie since [[Joe Smith (basketball)|Joe Smith]] in 1995–96 to post two 20–20 games in the same season. Blair also participated in the [[2010 NBA All-Star Game#Rookie Challenge|2010 Rookie Challenge]], where he recorded 22 points and 23 rebounds. [[Sacramento Kings]] guard [[Tyreke Evans]] won the game MVP award, but graciously offered to share it with Blair.<ref>{{cite web|first=Fran|last=Blinebury|url=http://www.nba.com/allstar/2010/rookie.challenge/index.html|title=Rookies break through in T-Mobile Rookie Challenge|work=NBA.com|date=February 13, 2010|access-date=January 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110318231647/http://www.nba.com/allstar/2010/rookie.challenge/index.html|archive-date=March 18, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> At the season's end, he was named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team and was the only Spurs player to appear in all 82 regular season games. He started 23 games, averaging 7.8 points and 6.4 rebounds in 18.2 minutes per game. He was also the top-ranked rookie in field goal percentage (.556), and was second in rebounding. Blair helped the Spurs defeat the Mavericks 4–2 in the first round of the playoffs, only to then go on to lose 4–0 to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the second round.

In 2010–11, Blair appeared in 81 games, including 65 starts, averaging 8.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 1.17 steals, and 1.0 assist in 21.4 minutes per game. He scored in double figures 28 times, including two 20-plus games, and posted 17 double-doubles, with 12 of those coming after the turn of the new year.

In September 2011, Blair signed with [[BC Krasnye Krylya]] of Russia for the duration of the [[2011 NBA lockout]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=aw-wojnarowski_dejuan_blair_russia_090211|title=Spurs' Blair to play in Russia during lockout|work=Sportando.com|date=September 2, 2011|access-date=September 2, 2011}}</ref> He was released by the club the following month after appearing in six games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/88663/krasnye-krylya-samara-released-dejuan-blair.html|title=Krasnye Krylya Samara released DeJuan Blair|work=Sportando.com|date=October 12, 2011|access-date=October 12, 2011}}</ref> He subsequently returned to the Spurs in December and in [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12]], he averaged 9.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in 64 games.

The addition of [[Boris Diaw]] and emergence of [[Tiago Splitter]] led to reduced playing time for Blair and, ultimately, a loss of his starting position during the 2012–13 season. Blair made his displeasure clear as the season progressed and eventually played a minimal role in the Spurs' rotation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cardiachill.com/2013/5/29/4366778/dejuan-blair-san-antonio-spurs-contract-pitt-basketball-nba-playoffs-vs-memphis-grizzlies|title=Dejuan Blair not likely to return to San Antonio Spurs in 2013–14|work=CardiacHill.com|date=May 29, 2013|access-date=May 29, 2013}}</ref> The Spurs went on to become Western Conference champions, only to eventually fall 4–3 to the defending champion [[Miami Heat]] in the [[2013 NBA Finals]].

===Dallas Mavericks (2013–2014)===
On August 7, 2013, Blair signed a one-year deal with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/08/07/mavs-officially-sign-blair.ap/|title=Mavericks sign center Blair to one-year deal|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 7, 2013|access-date=August 7, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203230617/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/08/07/mavs-officially-sign-blair.ap/|archive-date=December 3, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2013–14, he averaged 6.4 points and 4.7 rebounds in 15.6 minutes of action, playing 78 games (13 starts) while shooting 53.4% (210-of-393 FGs) from the field.

===Washington Wizards (2014–2016)===
On July 16, 2014, Blair was acquired by the [[Washington Wizards]] in a sign-and-trade deal with the Mavericks, a deal that sent the rights to [[Emir Preldžić]] to the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite news|last=Parker|first=Brandon|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/wizards-insider/wp/2014/07/16/wizards-finalizing-deal-for-dejuan-blair-in-sign-and-trade-with-mavericks/|title=Wizards acquire DeJuan Blair in sign-and-trade with Mavericks|work=WashingtonPost.com|date=July 16, 2014|access-date=January 13, 2016}}</ref> In 2014–15, Blair appeared in a career-low 29 games (his previous was 61) and failed to make a start for the first time in his six-year career. He also didn't appear in any of the Wizards' 10 playoff games and was deactivated for most of them.<ref>{{cite news|last=Michael |first=J. |url=http://www.csnmidatlantic.com/basketball-washington-wizards/talk/grading-dejuan-blairs-play-2014-15-season |title=Grading DeJuan Blair's play for 2014–15 season |work=csnmidatlantic.com |date=June 14, 2015 |access-date=January 13, 2016 }}{{dead link|date=December 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

On February 18, 2016, Blair was traded, along with [[Kris Humphries]] and a [[Georgios Papagiannis|2016 protected first-round draft pick]], to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Markieff Morris]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-trade-morris-first-round-pick|title=Suns Acquire First-Round Pick, Blair, Humphries from Washington for Morris|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2016|access-date=February 18, 2016}}</ref> Four days later, he was waived by the Suns.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-waive-blair|title=Suns Waive Blair|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2016|access-date=February 22, 2016}}</ref>

===Jiangsu Monkey King (2016)===
On September 7, 2016, Blair signed with [[Jiangsu Monkey King]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/211255/dejuan-blair-signs-with-jiangsu-tonxi.html|title=DeJuan Blair signs with Jiangsu Tonxi|work=Sportando.com|date=September 7, 2016|access-date=September 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917020750/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/211255/dejuan-blair-signs-with-jiangsu-tonxi.html|archive-date=September 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/462065/Jiangsu-Tongxi-adds-Blair-to-their-roster|title=Jiangsu Tongxi adds Blair to their roster|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=September 7, 2016|access-date=September 7, 2016}}</ref> In late November 2016, he was cut by the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/218435/ike-diogu-agreed-to-a-deal-with-jiangsu-tongxi.html|title=Ike Diogu agreed to a deal with Jiangsu Tongxi|work=Sportando.com|date=November 25, 2016|access-date=January 4, 2017}}</ref> In 10 games for Jiangsu, he averaged 24.1 points and 13.6 rebounds per game.

===Texas Legends and Los Angeles D-Fenders (2017)===
On January 17, 2017, Blair was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-dejuan-blair/|title=Legends Acquire DeJuan Blair|work=NBA.com|date=January 17, 2017|access-date=January 17, 2017|archive-date=February 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203103337/http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-dejuan-blair/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 11, 2017, Blair was traded by the Legends to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] in exchange for a 2017 fourth-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/d-fenders-acquire-dejuan-blair-texas/|title=D-Fenders Acquire DeJuan Blair From Texas|work=DLeague.NBA.com|date=February 11, 2017|access-date=February 11, 2017|archive-date=February 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170212100301/http://dleague.nba.com/news/d-fenders-acquire-dejuan-blair-texas/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===San Lorenzo de Almagro (2017–2018)===
On December 14, 2017, Blair signed with [[San Lorenzo de Almagro (basketball)|San Lorenzo de Almagro]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Un ex NBA llega a Boedo|url=http://www.sanlorenzo.com.ar/basquet/noticias/1513294841_un-ex-nba-llega-a-boedo|access-date=December 16, 2017|work=sanlorenzo.com|date=December 14, 2017|language=es}}</ref>

===Austin Spurs (2018–2019)===
On October 20, 2018, Blair was selected by the [[Austin Spurs]] in the [[2018 NBA G League draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-select-connor-burchfield-in-the-2018-nba-g-league-draft/|title=Austin Spurs Select Connor Burchfield in the 2018 NBA G League Draft|work=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2018|access-date=October 20, 2018}}</ref> Blair was later included on Austin's training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-training-camp-roster/|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2018 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2018|access-date=October 22, 2018|archive-date=October 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181023120939/https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-announce-2018-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In Summer 2019, Blair signed a contract with Italian team [[U.S. Victoria Libertas Pallacanestro|Carpegna Prosciutti Basket Pesaro]], but his contract was voided by Pesaro after his appeal against a two year suspension for testing positive for oxymorphone-oxycodone was rejected by [[FIBA]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FIBA rejects DeJuan Blair's appeal vs. doping suspension, VL Pesaro voids contract |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fiba-rejects-dejuan-blairs-appeal-vs-doping-suspension-vl-pesaro-voids-contract/ |website=sportando.basketball |publisher=Sportando |access-date=22 August 2019 }}</ref>

==Overseas Elite (2017)==
In the summer of 2017, Blair joined two-time [[The Basketball Tournament]] defending champion [[Overseas Elite]]. On August 3, 2017, Blair's team, Overseas Elite won its third straight The Basketball Tournament championship with an 86–83 victory over Team Challenge ALS on ESPN.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thetournament.com/news/overseas-elite-completes-3-peat-defeat-team-challenge-als-86-83|date=August 4, 2017|title=OVERSEAS ELITE COMPLETES THE 3-PEAT, DEFEAT TEAM CHALLENGE ALS 86–83|work=thetournament.com|access-date=August 10, 2017|archive-date=August 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810210720/http://thetournament.com/news/overseas-elite-completes-3-peat-defeat-team-challenge-als-86-83|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Blair averaged 8.0 points and 4.4 rebounds while shooting 50% from the field in 16.2 minutes per game.
